name: Threadbare Compression Undershirt
description: A once-white compression underlayer now the color of old teeth, pilled across the chest and nearly translucent at one shoulder. Originally a Pragma BioSync base layer, the brand text has been scrubbed off with something abrasive, leaving a ghost-pale rectangle on the fabric. Still provides warmth and moisture management, barely.
functionality: Moisture-wicking base layer that traps body heat; better than nothing against Lake Michigan cold.
what_it_says: The person wearing this is making do with what they have — pride stripped down to function.
worn_by: anyone surviving a Meridian winter on a Tier 1 budget
story_hooks: The brand was scrubbed off deliberately — owning Pragma gear on the Shelf marks you as a target for the wrong people.
It still smells faintly of the medical-grade antiseptic used in Pragma clinics.
related_entities: Tessera Corponation ChronoMark VR-3 Passive Isotopic Citizen Tagging System

physical_description.visual_profile: A skeletal, worn compression base layer that clings to the torso like a second skin. The garment reads as humble and survival-focused, a medical-functional piece stripped of corporate identity. It hangs with the quiet defeat of something that has absorbed years of labor.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight across chest and shoulders, conforming precisely to muscle and bone. The fit has relaxed slightly at the collar and cuffs from repeated wear, creating a subtle sag that contradicts the intended snugness.
physical_description.primary_material: Original synthetic moisture-wicking blend (Pragma proprietary), now degraded and brittle at stress points. The fabric is thin enough to be semi-translucent in high-wear areas.
physical_description.texture: Heavy pilling across the chest and upper back from friction and age. Smooth in remaining intact patches. One shoulder shows transparent, almost gossamer texture from thinning. Abraded flat spot where branding was removed—rough and slightly frayed.
physical_description.color_scheme: Off-white to dingy cream overall, with darker coffee-stain discoloration around collar, underarms, and lower back. The de-branded rectangle is ghost-pale, a slightly lighter rectangle against the yellowed body.
physical_description.closures: None—pullover compression shirt with elastic-trim crew neck and fitted long sleeves. Cuffs show stretched elastic.
distinctive_features: Aggressive de-branding: abraded rectangular scar where Pragma logo was removed
Transparent panel at right shoulder from thinning
Staining and discoloration indicating years of wear
Stretched elastic at neck and cuffs
No visible patches—owner chose to keep wearing rather than repair
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 salvage/sub-grade. This is survival wear, not fashion.
physical_description.cultural_context: Working poor or ungoverned sector. Someone who stripped corporate branding to reclaim the garment as their own. Suggests labor-intensive work, lack of resources for replacement, and subtle resistance to corpo identity markers.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily worn, degraded but still functional. The kind of piece that gets washed in sink water and air-dried on a radiator. No attempt at preservation—purely utilitarian.
